{
 "cwd": "/workspace",
 "query": "ULTRA WEBSITE BRIEF – LIGHTDOCS PUBLISHING SAAS DOCUMENTATION SITE

Create a polished, modern, fully responsive STATIC documentation + marketing website for a fictional SaaS product called "DraftNest". DraftNest is a publishing workflow platform for editorial teams, indie magazines, newsletters, and content studios. The website should feel like a clean documentation hub mixed with a SaaS landing page. Use React + Tailwind CSS. Everything must be static only: use mock/sample content, no backend, no login, no API calls, no database, no authentication, no real integrations.

GENERAL STYLE
- Overall style: light mode, airy, professional, readable, high trust
- Inspiration/reference feeling: Reddit-style community layout cues, especially compact cards, upvote-like visual accents, nested discussion previews, pill tags, sidebars, post/document lists, but do NOT copy Reddit branding
- Domain: publishing / editorial SaaS / documentation site
- Mood: calm, organized, friendly, slightly community-driven
- Colors: warm white background, soft gray panels, ink black text, muted orange/coral accent, blue secondary accent, subtle green success badges
- Typography: modern sans-serif, strong hierarchy, readable docs body text
- Use Tailwind utility classes, clean components, responsive from mobile to desktop
- Add tasteful cursor effects: soft spotlight glow following cursor on hero/docs cards, subtle hover trails or magnetic button hover. Keep it lightweight CSS/JS only, no canvas, no WebGL, no 3D.

MAIN GOAL
Build a static documentation website that explains the DraftNest SaaS product and its publishing workflow. It should look like a real product docs site with navigation, docs categories, quickstart, sample pages, changelog, community-style cards, FAQ, and call-to-action areas. All content can be fake but realistic.

PAGE STRUCTURE

1. TOP NAVIGATION
- Sticky top nav with logo: DraftNest
- Nav links: Docs, Guides, Templates, Changelog, Community, Pricing
- Search-looking input: "Search docs..." but static only, no functional search required
- CTA button: "Start Reading"
- Mobile hamburger menu is nice if possible, but static responsive layout is enough
- Add a small status pill: "v2.4 Docs"

2. HERO SECTION
- Big headline: "Documentation for publishing teams that ship faster."
- Subtitle: explain that DraftNest helps editors, writers, and reviewers organize drafts, approvals, style guides, and release notes in one calm workspace
- CTA buttons: "Read the Quickstart" and "Browse Templates"
- Right side: mock documentation preview card with tabs: Quickstart, Workflow, Review
- Add small Reddit-inspired document cards: title, tags, fake upvote count, comment count, last updated
- Add cursor spotlight effect over hero area

3. TRUST / USE CASE STRIP
- Horizontal row of fictional teams: Northline Review, Paperstack Studio, The Weekly Fold, Atlas Journal, InkRoom
- Below it include 3 short use cases:
  - Editorial calendars
  - Draft approvals
  - Style guide documentation

4. DOCS LAYOUT SECTION
Create a realistic documentation dashboard layout:
- Left sidebar categories:
  - Getting Started
  - Workspace Setup
  - Editorial Workflow
  - Publishing Templates
  - Reviewer Notes
  - Changelog
- Main content panel showing a "Quickstart" article with headings, paragraphs, bullet lists, code-like command blocks but not real backend setup
- Right sidebar "On this page" with anchors:
  - Create a workspace
  - Invite collaborators
  - Import sample drafts
  - Publish your first guide
- Add realistic docs cards and breadcrumbs
- Include a note callout, warning callout, and tip callout

5. FEATURE CARDS
Section title: "Everything your editorial docs need"
Cards with icons or simple emoji/icon placeholders:
- Structured Draft Libraries
- Review Checklists
- Version Notes
- Template Packs
- Approval Paths
- Public Knowledge Base
- Community Threads
- Markdown Friendly
Each card should have title, short description, and tiny tag label. Use hover states and cursor glow effect.

6. COMMUNITY-STYLE KNOWLEDGE FEED
Inspired by Reddit layout but branded differently:
- Section title: "Popular docs from the DraftNest community"
- Feed cards with static sample posts:
  - "How we structure issue planning for a monthly magazine"
  - "Template: 3-step editorial approval checklist"
  - "Best way to document recurring newsletter sections"
  - "Style guide example for multi-author publications"
- Each card has fake score, tag pills, comment count, reading time, author initials avatar
- Include a right sidebar with "Trending Topics": Style Guides, Review Loops, Newsletter Ops, Print Deadlines, Contributor Onboarding
- No real community functionality, just static cards

7. TEMPLATE SHOWCASE
Create publishing templates grid:
- Magazine Issue Planner
- Newsletter Launch Checklist
- Editorial Style Guide
- Contributor Onboarding Guide
- Release Notes Template
- Content QA Checklist
Each template card should include sample category, short description, "Preview Template" static button

8. WORKFLOW TIMELINE
A horizontal or vertical timeline showing:
- Plan issue
- Assign draft
- Review changes
- Approve copy
- Publish notes
- Archive learnings
Use clean connected steps, badges, and small descriptions. Keep it elegant and static.

9. PRICING PREVIEW / STATIC SAAS PLANS
Even though it is a docs site, include a small pricing area:
- Starter Docs – Free
- Editorial Team – $18/editor
- Publishing Studio – $49/editor
Use static pricing cards only, no checkout, no payment, no account creation. Buttons can say "View Plan Details".

10. CHANGELOG SECTION
Mock changelog cards:
- v2.4 – Template bundles and reviewer notes
- v2.3 – Faster docs navigation
- v2.2 – Public guide improvements
Include date, label, bullet updates. No dynamic data.

11. FAQ SECTION
Questions:
- Is this a real publishing platform?
- Can I use the templates for newsletters?
- Does DraftNest support Markdown?
- Can I publish public docs?
- Is the demo connected to a backend?
Answers should clarify this website is a static presentation/demo with sample content where appropriate.

12. FINAL CTA
Headline: "Build calmer publishing documentation."
Subtitle: "Give writers, editors, and reviewers one place to understand the process."
Buttons: "Open Documentation" and "Explore Templates"
Add decorative floating cards around CTA.

13. FOOTER
Columns:
- Product: Docs, Templates, Changelog, Pricing
- Resources: Guides, Community, Examples, Support
- Company: About, Editorial Blog, Contact
- Legal: Privacy, Terms
Include small line: "Static demo website using sample content."

DESIGN DETAILS
- Use Tailwind CSS only for styling
- Light theme only, no dark mode toggle needed
- Rounded corners, subtle shadows, thin borders, soft gradients
- Great spacing and alignment
- Make it feel premium but not over-designed
- Use responsive grids and stacked mobile layout
- Include empty/static search bar visual but no working search logic required
- Cursor effect should be subtle and performance-friendly: e.g. a small radial gradient glow that follows pointer and appears over interactive cards/hero
- Use realistic sample copy, not lorem ipsum
- Do not use external APIs, no backend, no authentication, no database, no live data, no CRUD, no realtime features
- No 3D, no WebGL, no canvas, no games
- Static mock content is enough

DELIVERABLE
A complete static React + Tailwind website for DraftNest with polished layout, realistic documentation content, SaaS publishing theme, Reddit-inspired community/document card patterns, and cursor hover/spotlight effects. It should run as a normal static front-end page without any external services.",

"""Grade a Webdev task as the explorer does (verl recipes/design webdev-eval): render, shrink, judge.

No index.html in dist/ scores 0. A render that fails, or a judge that never answers, writes no reward (not scored):
neither says anything about the page."""
import base64
import io
import json
import os
import random
import subprocess
import sys
import time
import urllib.request
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, "/tests")
os.environ["WEBDEV_GRADE_HTTP"] = "1"   # serve over loopback http so React/Vue/ES-module sites actually run
from webdev.eval_rubric import build_prompt  # noqa: E402
from webdev.shot import _build_shot_cmd, _parse_render_env, _parse_shot_b64  # noqa: E402
from webdev.verdict import parse_verdict  # noqa: E402

cfg = json.loads(Path("/tests/grade.json").read_text())
V = Path("/logs/verifier")
V.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
dist = Path(cfg["cwd"]) / "dist"


def done(reward: float | None, why: str, **extra) -> None:
    (V / "result.json").write_text(json.dumps({"reward": reward, "summary": why, **extra}, indent=1))
    print(why)
    if reward is None:
        print("not scored", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)
    (V / "reward.txt").write_text(f"{reward}\n")
    sys.exit(0)


files = sorted(str(p.relative_to(dist)) for p in dist.rglob("*") if p.is_file())[:200] if dist.is_dir() else []
if "index.html" not in files:
    done(0.0, "The agent delivered nothing to dist/." if not files else "dist/ has no index.html, so there is no page to open.",
         delivered=files)
res = subprocess.run(["sh", "-c", _build_shot_cmd(f"file://{dist}/index.html")], capture_output=True, text=True,
                     timeout=150)   # SHOT_TIMEOUT_S
shot = {"output": (res.stdout or "") + "\n" + (res.stderr or "")}
shot_b64, console_errors = _parse_shot_b64(shot)
render_env = _parse_render_env(shot)
if render_env.get("proxy_failed") or not shot_b64:
    print(shot["output"][-2000:], file=sys.stderr)
    done(None, "external assets were unreachable on every route" if render_env.get("proxy_failed")
         else "the screenshot produced no image")
jpg = base64.b64decode(shot_b64)
try:   # eval_mode._shrink: the judge refuses shots over 20 MP; proportional, quality 75
    from PIL import Image
    Image.MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS = None
    im = Image.open(io.BytesIO(jpg))
    size = im.size
    if im.width * im.height > 20e6:
        k = (20e6 / (im.width * im.height)) ** 0.5
        im = im.convert("RGB").resize((max(1, int(im.width * k)), max(1, int(im.height * k))), Image.LANCZOS)
        b = io.BytesIO(); im.save(b, "JPEG", quality=75); jpg = b.getvalue(); size = im.size
except ImportError:
    size = None
(V / "screenshot.jpg").write_bytes(jpg)
# webdev-structural-gate@1: necessary conditions, not a replacement judge.
_gate_layout = {}
for _line in (shot["output"] or "").splitlines():
    if _line.startswith("LAYOUT:"):
        try:
            _gate_layout = json.loads(_line[len("LAYOUT:"):])
        except (ValueError, TypeError):
            pass
        break
if (not isinstance(_gate_layout, dict) or _gate_layout.get("error")
        or not isinstance(_gate_layout.get("text"), str)
        or not isinstance(_gate_layout.get("scroll_w"), (int, float))
        or not isinstance(_gate_layout.get("client_w"), (int, float))
        or _gate_layout["client_w"] <= 0):
    done(None, "Structural measurements unavailable; not scored.")
_gate_text = " ".join(_gate_layout["text"].split())
_gate_kw = cfg.get("gate_keywords") or []
_gate_fails = []
if not _gate_text:
    _gate_fails.append("blank rendered DOM")
if _gate_kw and not any(_kw.casefold() in _gate_text.casefold() for _kw in _gate_kw):
    _gate_fails.append("no brief-keyword DOM presence")
if _gate_layout["scroll_w"] > _gate_layout["client_w"] + 1:
    _gate_fails.append("horizontal overflow")
_gate_report = {"passed": not _gate_fails, "failed": _gate_fails,
                "dom_chars": len(_gate_text), "keywords": _gate_kw,
                "layout": _gate_layout}
(V / "structural_gates.json").write_text(json.dumps(_gate_report, indent=1))
if _gate_fails:
    done(0.0, "Structural gates failed: " + "; ".join(_gate_fails),
         structural_gates=_gate_fails)
content = [{"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": "data:image/jpeg;base64," + base64.b64encode(jpg).decode()}},
           {"type": "text", "text": build_prompt().format(query=cfg["query"][:1500])}]   # QUERY_CAP
url = os.environ.get("WEBDEV_JUDGE_URL", "https://router.huggingface.co/v1").rstrip("/") + "/chat/completions"
_judge_pin = cfg["judge"]
if os.environ.get("WEBDEV_JUDGE_REVISION") != _judge_pin["model_sha"]:
    done(None, "Judge deployment revision is unbound; not scored.")
(V / "judge_config.json").write_text(json.dumps(_judge_pin, indent=1))
body = json.dumps({"model": cfg["judge"]["request_model"], "temperature": 0, "max_tokens": 1024,  # webdev-temp0-pin@1
                   "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": content}]}).encode()
verdict, last = None, ""
for attempt in range(4):   # JUDGE_RETRIES, with eval_mode's backoff
    if attempt:
        time.sleep(min(60.0, 3.0 * (3 ** (attempt - 1))) * (0.5 + random.random()))
    try:
        req = urllib.request.Request(url, data=body, method="POST", headers={
            "Content-Type": "application/json", "Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ.get('WEBDEV_JUDGE_KEY', '')}"})
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=180) as r:   # JUDGE_TIMEOUT_S
            _judge_reply = json.loads(r.read())
            if _judge_reply.get("model_revision") != _judge_pin["model_sha"]:
                done(None, "Judge response revision differs from the task pin; not scored.")
            msg = _judge_reply["choices"][0]["message"]
        v = parse_verdict(msg.get("content") or msg.get("reasoning_content") or "")
        if "_failed" not in v:
            verdict = v
            break
        last = v["_failed"]
    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
        last = f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}"[:200]
if not verdict:
    done(None, f"judge unavailable: {last}")
done(verdict["score"], verdict.get("reason", ""), dims=verdict["dims"], visual=verdict["visual"], screenshot_size=size,
     console_errors=console_errors[:1500] if console_errors not in ("", "[]") else "")

rationale: Gate trivial, off-brief and overflowing pages to a scored 0 before the vision call, cutting judge spend and the blank-page lottery. Passing pages reach the judge unchanged.

gate_keywords: Documentation for publishing teams that ship faster.
